We're gonna try exploring and proving with data whether legengaries are truly more
powerful on average. (we'll also take a look at mythicals)

We're going to do a pretty rudimentary analysis, every Pokémon has six base stats 
(HP, Attack, Defense, Special Attack, Special Defense and Speed). 
We're going to add these to get a **base stat total (BST)**, which we treat as a rough
measure of how strong a Pokémon is. Legendary Pokémon are supposed to be the strongest 
in the game, so this should help us get an idea of  how big the gap is.

## Data

The data is from [PokeAPI](https://pokeapi.co/)'s open dataset, taken from
this repository: [GitHub](https://github.com/PokeAPI/pokeapi/tree/master/data/v2/csv)

I use two tables: `pokemon_species.csv` (one row per species, with legendary
and mythical flags) and `pokemon_stats.csv` (one row per Pokémon per stat).

```{python}
#| label: load-data
#| message: false
#| warning: false
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

species = pd.read_csv("../../data/pokeapi/pokemon_species.csv")
pokemon_stats = pd.read_csv("../../data/pokeapi/pokemon_stats.csv")

pokemon_stats.head()
```

## Calculating base stat totals

Each Pokémon has six rows in `pokemon_stats`, so summing `base_stat` by
`pokemon_id` gives its BST. We then merge that with the species table. Each
species' default form has the same ID as the species, while alternate forms
(like Mega evolutions) have IDs above 10000, so the merge keeps exactly one
row per species.

```{python}
#| label: compute-bst
bst = pokemon_stats.groupby("pokemon_id")["base_stat"].sum().reset_index(name="bst")
df = species.merge(bst, left_on="id", right_on="pokemon_id")

df["group"] = "Regular"
df.loc[df["is_legendary"] == 1, "group"] = "Legendary"
df.loc[df["is_mythical"] == 1, "group"] = "Mythical"

df[["identifier", "generation_id", "bst", "group"]].head()
```

## Comparing the groups

```{python}
#| label: tbl-bst-by-group
#| tbl-cap: "Base stat total summary for regular, legendary and mythical Pokémon."
summary = df.groupby("group")["bst"].agg(["count", "mean", "median", "min", "max"])
summary.round(1)
```

@tbl-bst-by-group shows legendary and mythical Pokémon average roughly 180
more base stat points than regular Pokémon. Most of the 1,025 species are
regular, while legendary and mythical Pokémon together make up fewer than 100.

```{python}
#| label: fig-bst-hist
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of base stat totals for regular Pokémon compared with legendary and mythical Pokémon."
#| fig-alt: "Two overlapping histograms of base stat total. Regular Pokémon are spread between roughly 200 and 600; legendary and mythical Pokémon are concentrated between 550 and 720."
bins = range(150, 751, 25)
special = df[df["group"] != "Regular"]
regular = df[df["group"] == "Regular"]

ax = regular["bst"].plot.hist(bins=bins, alpha=0.6, label="Regular")
special["bst"].plot.hist(bins=bins, alpha=0.6, label="Legendary / Mythical", ax=ax)
ax.set_xlabel("Base stat total")
ax.set_ylabel("Number of Pokémon")
ax.legend()
plt.show()
```

## Takeaways

The histogram pretty clearly shows that there's a stark difference in base stats between the 2 groups. 
Regular Pokémon mostly show up between about 200 and 600 while legendaries and mythicals are concentrated at the larger values.
